name: Re-speaking evaluation metrics
description: Re-speaking is a mechanism for obtaining high quality subtitles for use in live broadcast and other public events. Because it relies on humans performing the actual re-speaking, the task of estimating the quality of the results is non-trivial. Most organisations rely on humans to perform the actual quality assessment, but purely automatic methods have been developed for other similar problems, like Machine Translation. This paper will try to compare several of these methods: BLEU, EBLEU, NIST, METEOR, METEOR-PL, TER and RIBES. These will then be matched to the human-derived NER metric, commonly used in re-speaking.
reputation: A niche but useful benchmark for comparing automatic subtitle-quality metrics against human re-speaking judgments.
notes: Non-LLM benchmark focused on metric comparison rather than model generation; likely small and domain-specific, with results depending on correlation to human NER rather than a single universal score.
